# Preschool

::: {.ctg-box}
**This topic aligns with [Closing the Gap Outcome Area 3](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/dashboard/outcome-area/early-childhood-education/): Children are engaged in high quality, culturally appropriate early childhood education in their early years**

Target: By 2025, increase the proportion of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children enrolled in Year Before Full-Time Schooling (YBFS) early childhood education to 95%.
:::

:::{style="height: 1em;"}
:::

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Preschool enrollments
# Data from Victorian Child and Adolescent Monitoring System
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in VCAMS data
childhood_enrol <- readxl::read_xlsx(file.path(root_folder, subfolder_vcams, "VCAMS_indicator_4_3c.xlsx"), 
                                     sheet        = "4.3c 2018 onwards", 
                                     trim_ws      = TRUE, 
                                     .name_repair = "universal_quiet") %>% 
  #
  janitor::clean_names()

# Data wrangling
childhood_enrol <- childhood_enrol %>%
  dplyr::select(year,
                aboriginal_n = numerator,
                aboriginal_prop = indicator_calc) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(aboriginal_prop = aboriginal_prop * 100)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Preschool attendance
# Data from CtG Information Repository
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NECECC data
childhood_attendance <- readxl::read_excel(file.path(root_folder, subfolder_ctg, "CTG03_Childhood_Education_Data_Tables.xlsx"),
                                           skip  = 1,
                                           sheet = "Table SE3a.1") %>% 
    janitor::clean_names() %>% 
    #
    dplyr::rename(value = x3,
                  indigenous_status = x4,
                  year = x5,
                  attendance = x6) %>%
    #
    tidyr::fill(value, indigenous_status, year, attendance) %>% 
    #
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(vic)) %>%
    #
    dplyr::select(value,
                  year,
                  indigenous_status,
                  attendance,
                  vic)

# Data wrangling
childhood_attendance <- childhood_attendance %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(vic = as.numeric(vic),
                #
                attendance = factor(dplyr::case_when(
                  attendance == "Did not attend"            ~ "Did not attend",
                  attendance == "One to less than 10 hours" ~ "<10 hours",
                  attendance == "10–14 hours"               ~ "10-14 hours",
                  attendance == "15 hours or more"          ~ "15+ hours",
                  #
                  TRUE ~ NA_character_),
                  #
                  levels = c("Did not attend",
                             "<10 hours",
                             "10-14 hours",
                             "15+ hours")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [Victorian Child and Adolescent Monitoring System (VCAMS)](https://www.vic.gov.au/victorian-child-and-adolescent-monitoring-system-vcams) and the [Closing the Gap Information Repository](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/).

- In 2022, 100% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children in Victoria who were in the year before full-time schooling age cohort attended a funded kindergarten/preschool program. This is above the Closing the Gap target of 95%.

- The percentage of enrolled children who attended for 15 or more hours in a week increased from 64% in 2016 to 75% in 2023.

**Key points from stakeholder consultation**

- At stakeholder consultations during the development of this report the impact of the scaling up of free kindergarten to 15 hours per week in 2022 was discussed as a potential contributing factor to rising preschool attendance.

- The importance of and impact of improvements in cultural safety by educators was also discussed as a potential contributing factor to this increase.

```{r}
#
figure_number <- childhood_enrol %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(hover_text = paste0(year, "\n",
                                    "Count: ", format(aboriginal_n, big.mark = ","))) %>%
  #
  f_line_simple(y_variable = aboriginal_n,
                y_max      = NA,
                y_breaks   = 200,
                y_expand   = 75,
                y_title    = "Number of children")

figure_percent <- childhood_enrol %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(hover_text = paste0(year, "\n",
                                    "Percentage: ", sprintf("%.1f", aboriginal_prop))) %>%
  #
  f_line_simple(y_variable = aboriginal_prop,
                y_max      = 100,
                y_breaks   = 10,
                y_expand   = 1,
                y_title    = "Percentage of children",
                ctg_target = 95)

f_line_simple_combine(figure_number, figure_percent)
```

::: {.callout-note title="Data notes" icon=false collapse=false}
- Data for Figure 6B-1 and Table 6B-1 were obtained from the [Victorian Child and Adolescent Monitoring System (VCAMS)](https://www.vic.gov.au/victorian-child-and-adolescent-monitoring-system-vcams).
  - VCAMS brings together data from a wide range of sources about early childhood, family functioning, and communities to monitor and report against the indicators in the VCAMS Outcomes Framework.
  - This indicator uses the “year before school” population as the denominator. This is a proportion of all 4 and 5 year old children which reflects the age composition of the cohort of children who are in the year before starting school during a single calendar year. These calculations are based on the [ABS Estimated Residential Population](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/population/population-projections-australia/2022-base-2071), which takes into account the known under-reporting of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander status in the Census.

:::{style="height: 1em;"}
:::

- Data for Figure 6B-2 and Table 6B-2 were obtained from the [Closing the Gap Information Repository](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/) compiled from the [National Early Childhood Education and Care Collection (NECECC)](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/education/preschool-education/latest-release).
  - The Closing the Gap Information Repository brings together data from a wide range of data sources to provide up to date information for each Closing the Gap target, indicator, and contextual factors.
  - The NECECC collates data on preschool enrollments, attendance, and service providers from the Australian Government, state and territory education departments, and the Catholic Education Office of the Archdiocese of Canberra and Goulburn. The NECEEC conducts an annual census on the first Friday in August, with the reference week for data collection being the week before the census date.
  - Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children are defined as those who were identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander by a parent or guardian.
  - Data were not available for 2020 and 2021 due to the impact of COVID restrictions on preschool program delivery in Victoria.

:::{style="height: 1em;"}

# Early Childhood Development

::: {.ctg-box}
**This topic aligns with [Closing the Gap Outcome Area 4](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/dashboard/outcome-area/children-thriving/): Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children thrive in their early years**

Target: By 2031, increase the proportion of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children assessed as developmentally on track in all five domains of the Australian Early Development Census (AEDC) to 55%.
:::

:::{style="height: 1em;"}
:::

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Early childhood development
# Data from CtG Information Repository
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in AEDC data
childhood_develop <- readxl::read_excel(file.path(root_folder, subfolder_ctg, "CTG04_Early_Years_Data_Tables.xlsx"),
                                        skip  = 1,
                                        sheet = "Table CtG4A.1") %>% 
  janitor::clean_names() %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(indigenous_status = x3,
                year = x4) %>%
  #
  tidyr::fill(indigenous_status, year) %>%
  #
  dplyr::filter(row_number() %in% 1:14) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(vic)) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(indigenous_status,
                year,
                vic)

# Data wrangling
childhood_develop <- childhood_develop %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    vic = as.numeric(vic),
    #
    year = dplyr::case_when(year == "2009 (b)" ~ "2009",
                            TRUE ~ year),
    #
    indigenous_label = dplyr::case_when(
      indigenous_status == "Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children" ~ "Aboriginal",
      indigenous_status == "Non-Indigenous children"                        ~ "Non-Indigenous",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_),
    #
    indigenous_status = factor(dplyr::case_when(
      indigenous_label == "Aboriginal"     ~ "Identified as Aboriginal\nand/or Torres Strait Islander",
      indigenous_label == "Non-Indigenous" ~ "Did not identify as Aboriginal\nand/or Torres Strait Islander",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_),
      #
      levels = c("Identified as Aboriginal\nand/or Torres Strait Islander",
                 "Did not identify as Aboriginal\nand/or Torres Strait Islander")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [Closing the Gap Information Repository](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/).

- In 2021, 36% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children in Victoria who were assessed during their first year of school were developmentally on track for all five AEDC domains, compared to 32% in 2009.   

- This is below the Closing the Gap target of 55%, and is lower than for non-Indigenous children in 2021 (58%).

**Key points from stakeholder consultation**

- At stakeholder consultations during the development of this report, a lack of culturally safe and accessible health services for the diagnosis of childhood health issues was cited as a possible barrier.

- For example, whilst a very high proportion of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander babies have their hearing screened at birth, middle ear infections and associated hearing problems are a common childhood issue for First Nations children.

# Childhood Numeracy and Literacy

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Childhood literacy - reading
# Data from NAPLAN
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NAPLAN data
naplan_reading <- f_read_naplan(data_sheet = "Table SE5c.1")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Childhood literacy - writing
# Data from NAPLAN
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NAPLAN data
naplan_writing <- f_read_naplan(data_sheet = "Table SE5c.2")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Childhood numeracy
# Data from NAPLAN
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NAPLAN data
naplan_numeracy <- f_read_naplan(data_sheet = "Table SE5c.3")
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [National Assessment Program — Literacy and Numeracy (NAPLAN) program](https://www.acara.edu.au/reporting/national-report-on-schooling-in-australia/naplan-national-results), administered by the Australian Curriculum, Assessment, and Reporting Authority (ACARA).

- In 2024, 75% of Victorian Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children in Year 3, 78% of children in Year 5, 74% of children in Year 7, and 72% of children in Year 9 were at or above the NAPLAN reading minimum standard (exceeding, strong, or developing). This was lower than for non-Indigenous children at each year level (Year 3 = 90%, Year 5 = 93%, Year 7 = 92%, Year 9 = 90%).

- In 2024, 81% of Victorian Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children in Year 3, 78% of children in Year 5, 75% of children in Year 7, and 72% of children in Year 9 were at or above the NAPLAN writing minimum standard (exceeding, strong, or developing). This was lower than for non-Indigenous children at each year level (Year 3 = 94%, Year 5 = 93%, Year 7 = 92%, Year 9 = 90%).

- In 2024, 75% of Victorian Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children in Year 3, 75% of children in Year 5, 72% of children in Year 7, and 69% of children in Year 9 were at or above the NAPLAN numeracy minimum standard (exceeding, strong, or developing). This was lower than for non-Indigenous children at each year level (Year 3 = 91%, Year 5 = 92%, Year 7 = 91%, Year 9 = 90%).

### Figure 6B-6

::: {#fig_6B_6 .fig-tab-title}
**Figure 6B-6:** Percentage of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children at each NAPLAN numeracy proficiency level, Victoria, 2024
:::

```{r}
#
naplan_numeracy %>%
  dplyr::filter(indigenous_status == "Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(hover_text = paste0(grade, "\n",
                                    achievement, "\n",

                fill_values   = c(colour_stackgrey, colour_stack4, colour_stack3, colour_stack2, colour_stack1),
                y_max         = 102,
                y_breaks      = 10,
                y_expand      = 1,
                y_title       = "Percentage of children")
```

**Table 6B-6:** Percentage of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children at each NAPLAN numeracy proficiency level, Victoria, 2024
:::

```{r}
#
table_count  <- table_count + 1
table_number <- paste0("Table_", table_section, "_", sprintf("%.02d", table_count))

table_headers <- c("Proficiency level",
                   "Year 3",
                   "Year 5",
                   "Year 7",
                   "Year 9")

table <- naplan_numeracy %>% 
  dplyr::filter(indigenous_status == "Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students") %>%
  #
  dplyr::select(-indigenous_status,
                -year) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from  = "grade",
                     values_from = "vic") %>% 
  #
  janitor::clean_names() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals()

if (!file.exists(paste0(here::here(), "/data/", table_number, ".csv"))) {
  
  write.csv(table, paste0(here::here(), "/data/", table_number, ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  
}

table %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(year_3 = sprintf("%.1f", year_3),
                year_5 = sprintf("%.1f", year_5),
                year_7 = sprintf("%.1f", year_7),
                year_9 = sprintf("%.1f", year_9)) %>% 
  #
  f_table_simple(total_row     = nrow(table),
                 table_headers = table_headers) %>% 
  #
  kableExtra::column_spec(2:5,
                          width = "1in")
```
